The '''Terry Fox Run''' is an annual non-competitive charity event held around the world to raise money for [[cancer research]]
in commemoration of Canadian [[cancer]] activist [[Terry Fox]] and his [[Marathon of Hope]].

The event was founded in 1981 by [[Isadore Sharp]], who had contacted Terry in hospital by telegram and expressed his wishes to hold an annual run in Terry's name to raise funds for cancer research. Sharp had lost his son to cancer in 1979. The event is held every year on the second Sunday following [[Labour Day]]. Since its inception, it has raised via the 'Terry Fox Foundation' over $750 million ([[Canadian dollar|CAD]]).<ref>{{cite web|title=Terry's Story|url=http://www.terryfox.org/terrys-story/|website=The Terry Fox Foundation|accessdate=28 January 2018}}</ref> The run is informal which means that the distance often varies, usually between 5 and 15 kilometres; participation is considered to be more important than completing the set distance. There are also runs set up by schools of every level, often with shorter distances than the "official" ones.

The Terry Fox Run has no corporate sponsorship, in accordance with Terry Fox's original wishes of not seeking fame or fortune from his endeavour.  During his cross-Canada run, he rejected every endorsement he was offered{{Citation Needed|date=April 2025}}, as he felt that it would detract from his goal of creating public awareness. The Terry Fox Runs have no advertisements on any race related materials (such as T-shirts, banners, etc.), and the Terry Fox Foundation's policies are explicitly against profiting from association with the charity goal of the run,<ref>{{cite web |title=Terry Fox Foundation Run Policies and Guidelines |url=https://terryfox.org/run-policies-guidelines/ |website=Terry Fox Foundation |access-date=22 April 2025}}</ref> though not-for-profit support is welcomed.<ref>{{cite web |title=A Marathon of Hope: The Terry Fox Story - adidas Group |url=https://www.adidas-group.com/en/magazine/behind-the-scenes/a-marathon-of-hope-the-terry-fox-story |website=Adidas |access-date=22 April 2025}}</ref>

==History==
[[File:TerryFoxToronto19800712.JPG|thumb|100px|left|Terry Fox]]
[[File:Terry Fox Run Milan.jpg|thumb|The Terry Fox Run in [[Milan]], Italy, in 2007]]
The Terry Fox Foundation<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.terryfox.org/ |title=A single dream, A world of hope |website=The Terry Fox Foundation}}</ref> was founded in 1988 after it separated from the [[Canadian Cancer Society]]. Since its inception, The Terry Fox Foundation has raised over $800 million for cancer research. Currently, Terry Fox Runs take place every year with many participants from all over the world. The Run is a volunteer led, all-inclusive, non-competitive event with no corporate sponsorship, incentives or fundraising minimums. Fox laid out these wishes before his death in 1981.

In 2007 The Terry Fox Foundation created the Terry Fox Research Institute<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.tfri.ca/index.asp |title=Terry Fox Research Institute - Home |website=Terry Fox Research Institute}}</ref> to conduct transnational research to significantly improve outcomes for cancer patients. In the fiscal year ending March 31, 2013, The Terry Fox Foundation directed $27.7 million to its cancer research programs.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.terryfox.org/Research/Terry_Fox_Foundation_Funded_Research.html |title=Terry Fox Foundation Research|website=The Terry Fox Foundation}}</ref>

The Terry Fox Foundation has expanded beyond the traditional Run as well, by holding various other events. These events include National School Run Day,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.terryfox.org/SchoolRun/ |title=National School Run Day |website=The Terry Fox Foundation}}</ref> where schools throughout Canada hold a Run to commemorate Fox and raise funds, and The Great Canadian Hair "Do",<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.terryfox.org/Works/ |title=Terry Fox Works |website=The Terry Fox Foundation}}</ref> which is a fundraising event that can take place at any time of the year. Participants are able to make the event as creative as they want— shave their heads, dye their hair a wacky colour, include a manly leg wax, and recruit friends to shave their heads as well.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/terry-fox-family-members-get-heads-shaved-for-cancer-research-1.687767 |title=Terry Fox family members get heads shaved for cancer research |website=CBC News}}</ref>

==Debuts by country==
* Canada – September 13, 1981, at 760 sites
* Cuba – 1998. In 2005, over 1.9 million people used 3,600 sites. In 2006, it had around 2.6 million participants. The tenth run in 2007 had 4,652 sites and 2.267 million runners.
* United States – 1990 in Bangor, Maine
*Venezuela – 1998 at the Colegio Internactional de Caracas
[[File:Terry Fox Run (1506100972).jpg|thumb|right|A runner's tag for a Terry Fox Run in Milan, Italy, in 2007]]
* Bulgaria – 2013 and 2017 at the Anglo-American School of Sofia
* Croatia – 2000<ref>{{cite web |url=http://pliva.hr/zajednica/vijesti/clanak/319/Terry-Fox-Run-odrzat-ce-se-17-rujna-na-Jarunu.html |title="Terry Fox Run" održat će se 17. rujna na Jarunu |website=PLIVA|language=hr}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.studentnet.hr/sport/show/1877/ |title=Terry Fox Run maraton na Jarunu |first=Boris |last=Jelavić |website=StudentNet |date=September 16, 2006|language=hr}}</ref>
* Hungary – 1999, ended in 2005
* Poland – 2006<ref>[http://www.tvn.pl/2006,10,1364333,nagoraco.html tvn.pl<!-- Bot generated title -->] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20061014033931/http://www.tvn.pl/2006,10,1364333,nagoraco.html |date=October 14, 2006 }}</ref>
* Portugal – 1994<ref>[https://wayback.archive-it.org/all/20081013012728/http://geo.international.gc.ca/canada-europa/portugal/embassy/terryfoxrun06-en.aspx Portugal :: Terry Fox Run<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref>
*Spain – 2017
* Oman – 2008<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.taism.com/community/annual-events/terry-fox-run |title=Carrying on the legacy of Terry Fox |website=TAISM}}</ref>
* Syria – 1991, ended after 2010 for civil war
[[File:Smiling boy at TFR 2014.jpg|thumb|200px|A happy moment at the TFR 2014 in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam (2014)]]
* Australia – September 1988 in [[Brisbane]] (legacy from Expo '88) raising $22,000 AUD
* China – 1998
* Hong Kong – 2013
* Malaysia – Early 1990s in [[Kuala Lumpur]]<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.terryfoxrunkl.org/ |title=Terry Fox Run Kuala Lumpur |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20071013020420/http://www.terryfoxrunkl.org/ |archivedate=October 13, 2007}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.facebook.com/TerryFoxRunKL |title=Terry Fox Run KL|website=[[Facebook]] }}</ref>
* New Zealand – 2023 in both [[Auckland]] and [[Christchurch]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Terry Fox Run NZ Raisly |url=https://terry-fox-run-nz.raisely.com/ }}</ref>
* Philippines – 2001 in [[Cebu City]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.philstar.com/cebu-sports/300708/terry-fox-run-kicks-today |title=Terry Fox Run kicks off today |date=October 8, 2005 |publisher=The Freeman |accessdate=April 12, 2012}}</ref>
* Taiwan – 2001 in [[Taipei City]]
* Thailand – 1995 in [[Bangkok]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.asiatraveltips.com/news05/310-CancerResearch.shtml |title=Bangkok's Eleventh Annual Terry Fox Run for Cancer Research to be held 30 October 2005 |accessdate=September 14, 2011}}</ref>
* Vietnam – 1996 in [[Ho Chi Minh City]]. In 2014, it drew about 16,500 participants and the organization committee included the [[Canadian Chamber of Commerce in Vietnam]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.canchamvietnam.org/ |title=18th Annual Terry Fox Run 2014 In HCMC |archiveurl=http://www.canchamvietnam.org/component/jcalpro/view/353/2.html?tmpl=component |archivedate=November 28, 2014}}</ref>
